name: Bangladesh
summary: East Bengal became East Pakistan in 1947 and won independence as Bangladesh in 1971 after a war; one of the most densely populated countries, a garment-export giant.

knownFor.label: Microcredit
knownFor.note: Grameen Bank loans to the poor.

location.value: The Ganges–Brahmaputra delta in South Asia; area 148,460 km² in the infobox and 148,461 km² in the text.

terrain.value: A flat, low-lying delta where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers meet and flow into the Bay of Bengal.

climate.value: Tropical monsoon, with hot, wet summers and cyclones, and a cooler dry winter.

resources.value: Fertile land for rice and jute, natural gas and fish.

population.value: 169,828,911 at the 2022 census. Later estimates disagree: 171,466,990 (World Bank, 2023), 175,423,000 (infobox, 2026) and “almost 177.8 million” (text).

urbanisation.value: Dhaka is one of the largest cities in the world.

disease.value: Cholera and diarrhoeal diseases occur, but child health and life expectancy have improved greatly since 1990.

migration.value: Rohingya refugees from Myanmar; workers in the Gulf.

economicBase.value: Over 84% of export earnings come from the textile industry; the page gives no separate garment-only share.

tradeRoutes.value: The port of Chittagong handles most trade, and garments are shipped to Europe and North America.

moneyAndTax.value: The taka; garment exports are a main source of foreign income.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A unitary parliamentary republic based on the Westminster system.

keyRulers.value: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman led the country until his assassination in 1975; Ziaur Rahman founded the BNP on 1 September 1978 and was assassinated in 1981. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Governments have changed through elections and coups; the 1975 and 1981 coups killed two presidents.

institutions.value: A parliament (Jatiya Sangsad), a presidency and local government.

stability.value: Coups (1975); protests ended the prime minister’s rule (2024).

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Armed forces that also serve as UN peacekeepers, among the largest contributors in the world.

majorWars.value: Liberation War: independence proclaimed on 26 March 1971, a provisional government on 10 April, and Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971, after about nine months.

alliancesRivals.value: Close to India, which helped in 1971, and increasingly to China.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: The University of Dhaka (1921) and many newer universities; literacy has grown strongly.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Rivers and ferries carry much traffic; the Padma Bridge (2022) links the south-west to Dhaka.

religion.value: 91.04% Muslim and 7.94% Hindu in the 2022 census (infobox).

languageWriting.value: Bengali; the Language Movement of 1952 for Bengali as a state language became a symbol of identity.

artsArchitecture.value: Baul songs, Bengali literature (including Rabindranath Tagore’s and Kazi Nazrul Islam’s works) and terracotta temples.

socialStructure.value: Mostly Bengali, with small Indigenous groups in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

sharedIdentity.value: Bengali language and the Liberation War.

dailyLife.value: Many families live in rural homes and eat rice and fish; dense cities such as Dhaka are crowded.

ideasReligions.value: Bengali nationalism drove the independence movement of 1971, and Islam is the majority faith.

colonisation.value: Part of British India until 1947, then Pakistan until 1971.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge. The textile industry gives over 84% of export earnings and has driven growth since the early 1990s; the prime minister was ousted on 5 August 2024 and an interim government followed.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Still in existence since independence on 16 December 1971. After the 2026 election the BNP returned to power, with Tarique Rahman prime minister from 17 February 2026.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
